title: Many Americans Won't Travel Without Their Pets
paragraphs: For many Americans, pets are an important part of the family. So, when they travel, they want to bring their pets with them. A new survey shows how much pets change people's travel plans.
The survey was done online by Talker Research for the car company Subaru in July 2026. It asked 2,000 American adults who drive and have cats or dogs about their travel plans.

The survey found that 68% of pet owners said their pet would change their travel plans this year. In addition, 45% said they had said no to a trip because they could not take their pet. And 73% said they were more likely to take a road trip by car than to fly, so they could bring their pet.
Some people even like traveling with their pets more than with other people. In the survey, 51% said they prefer to travel with a pet than with a person.
Young people travel with their pets the most. In the past five years, 75% of Gen Z pet owners and 70% of millennials took a road trip with their pet. But only 40% of baby boomers did.
When people travel by car with their pets, they want enough space for their pets and bags. They also want to be able to see their pets and to clean the seats easily.
Another survey by the company PetScreening found that almost half of pet owners had changed, shortened or canceled travel plans because they could not find a place to stay that allowed pets.
